__NOTOC__
'''Rulebooks''' and related documents record the development of the rules of ''Star Wars'' CCG. The game began with the [[Premiere starter deck rulebook|Premiere starter booklet]] in 1995. Expansion supplements added mechanics and revised existing procedures; online FAQs and ''Current Rulings'' answered questions between publications. [[Special Edition]] consolidated this material in Rulebook 2.0 and Glossary 2.0 in November 1998. Later supplements and the [[Players Committee]]’s Advanced Rulebook continued that process.<ref name="premiere-history">Decipher, ''The Rules'' (1995), [[Media:Decipher_Premiere_Starter_Deck_Rulebook_1995.pdf|Premiere starter deck rulebook]], pp. 1–40.</ref><ref name="glossary-history">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgglossary.pdf Glossary, Version 2.0], Decipher (November 1998), pp. 1–2, 32. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000903011039/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgglossary.pdf Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="pc-history">Players Committee, [[Media:AR-version-1-7-1.pdf|Advanced Rulebook 1.7.1]] (2007), introduction, printed p. vi.</ref>

The [[Rules document catalogue|full document catalogue]] provides the dated editions, original documents and wiki reading copies. For learning or playing today, see [[#Find the right rules|Find the right rules]] below.

== History of the rules ==

=== 1995–1996: the printed foundation and expansion supplements ===

The [[Premiere Limited]] starter decks included a 40-page booklet titled ''The Rules''. It explained the game’s card types, Force, turn sequence, movement and battles, and included its own glossary of terms. The later standalone Glossary grew beyond that original glossary into a much larger reference covering individual cards and detailed interactions.<ref name="premiere-history" /><ref name="glossary-history" />

[[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]]’s 1996 supplement added Immediate Effects, Used Or Lost Interrupts and rules for cumulative effects and undercover spies. Supplements also changed how existing cards were played. [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] reorganized location deployment into interior sites, docking bays, exterior sites and systems, with numbered marker sites determining the order of Hoth locations. Its new and revised rules superseded the corresponding Premiere and A New Hope rules.<ref name="anh-history">[http://www.decipher.com:80/starwars/productlibrary/rules/anhrules.pdf A New Hope Rules Supplement], Decipher (1996). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961219030729/http://www.decipher.com:80/starwars/productlibrary/rules/anhrules.pdf Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="hoth-history">[http://www.decipher.com:80/starwars/productlibrary/rules/hothrules.pdf Hoth Rules Supplement], Decipher (1996), p. 1. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961219030708/http://www.decipher.com:80/starwars/productlibrary/rules/hothrules.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

The Hoth supplement acknowledged the difficulty of overlapping documents. Decipher announced work on a second-edition booklet intended to organize the existing rules and eliminate inconsistency and outdated material.<ref name="hoth-history" />

[[File:Rulebook-2.0-location-layout.png|center|thumb|520px|Rulebook 2.0 location layout (1998), continuing Hoth’s deployment arrangement.]]

=== 1996: online rules and the FAQ ===

Online distribution accompanied the printed documents early in the game’s life. By December 1996, Decipher’s website offered expansion rules as PDFs and browsable HTML, with text and Word versions available through FTP. Premiere’s rules were also listed as an FTP text download.<ref name="web-history">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/rules/index.html Star Wars Customizable Card Game: Rules], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961219010259/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/rules/index.html Internet Archive, 19 December 1996].</ref>

The FAQ supplied answers alongside those rules. An A New Hope FAQ addendum was released on '''1 October 1996'''; its introduction acknowledged the size and uncertainty of the existing rulebook and FAQ and described work on a definitive rulebook. The FAQ introduction described a monthly release schedule, accompanied by an update containing the new and revised entries. Players could consult material online between printed releases.<ref name="faq96-history">[http://www.decipher.com:80/starwars/productlibrary/faqs/addendum.html FAQs Addendum Including A New Hope], Decipher (1 October 1996). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961219031200/http://www.decipher.com:80/starwars/productlibrary/faqs/addendum.html Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="faq-intro-history">[http://www.decipher.com:80/starwars/productlibrary/faqs/introduction.html Introduction to the FAQ], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961219031209/http://www.decipher.com:80/starwars/productlibrary/faqs/introduction.html Internet Archive].</ref>

=== 1997–1998: revised booklets, preliminary answers and Current Rulings ===

The booklet supplied with [[The Empire Strikes Back Introductory Two-Player Game]] contained all the Premiere rules and was their updated reference before Special Edition. Expansion supplements continued alongside it. [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] added special deployment and movement restrictions; [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] replaced the earlier sector rules; and [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba’s Palace]] introduced Starting Interrupts and amended the selection of starting locations.<ref name="early-index-history">[http://decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/rules/ Star Wars Customizable Card Game: Rules], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19980506111511/http://decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/rules/ Internet Archive, 6 May 1998].</ref><ref name="dagobah-history">[http://decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/rules/dagobahrules.pdf Dagobah Rules Supplement], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19980717034941/http://decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/rules/dagobahrules.pdf Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="cloud-city-history">[http://decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/rules/ccityrules.pdf Cloud City Rules Supplement], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19980717034823/http://decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/rules/ccityrules.pdf Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="jabbas-history">[http://decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/rules/jabbaspalacerules.pdf Jabba’s Palace Rules Supplement], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19980717034634/http://decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/rules/jabbaspalacerules.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

The FAQ rewrite appeared in partial preliminary releases on '''5 and 18 June 1997'''. The second release named the Empire Strikes Back booklet and First Anthology supplement as the current rules documents it supplemented and clarified. It described its answers as preliminary and subject to change, distinguished published FAQ answers from interim answers by Decipher representatives, and left tournament directors the final authority on rulings.<ref name="faq97-history">[http://decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/faqs/faq061897.pdf Frequently Asked Questions: Second Partial Preliminary FAQ], Decipher (18 June 1997), p. 1 and Captain Khurgee entry. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19980717002749/http://decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/faqs/faq061897.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

The '''24 April 1998 Current Rulings''' document continued that work while the full FAQ rewrite was underway. Its alphabetical entries used a source key to distinguish FAQ material, partial preliminary answers, rulings and new rulings. This was a growing body of interpretations and clarifications alongside the rules booklets and expansion supplements.<ref name="cr98-history">[http://decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/faqs/42498swcurrules.pdf Current Rulings], Decipher (24 April 1998), p. 1 and Captain Khurgee entry. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19980717002635/http://decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/faqs/42498swcurrules.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

=== November 1998: Special Edition consolidates rules, rulings and card text ===

[[Special Edition]] provided both [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game RULEBOOK 2.0|Rulebook 2.0]] and [[Decipher Glossary 2.0|Glossary 2.0]] in its starter decks. The rulebook replaced earlier rules documents, and the Glossary replaced the FAQ. The Glossary’s introduction recommended discarding the pre-November 1998 booklets, supplements, FAQs and Current Rulings in favour of the new reference.<ref name="se-index-history">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/rules/index.html Star Wars Customizable Card Game: Rules], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990428184433/http://www.decipher.com:80/starwars/productlibrary/rules/index.html Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="glossary-history" />

The two documents had complementary purposes: the rulebook explained play, while the 142-page alphabetical Glossary brought together rules concepts, card entries, detailed interactions and revised game text. It also changed gameplay. Its highlighted changes included allowing characters, vehicles and starships to carry multiple weapons and devices, even duplicates; limiting each Jedi-training mentor to one apprentice at a time; and revising long-range weapons and creature rules.<ref name="glossary-history" />

The Glossary distinguished replacement wording intended to clarify existing play from seventeen revisions explicitly marked '''Errata''' that changed gameplay. It stated that the supplied game text governed all versions of the affected cards from November 1998. Some revised wording also appeared on the white-bordered A New Hope and Hoth reprints. A printed card could therefore remain usable while its applicable text was supplied by a later document.<ref name="glossary-history" />

[[Captain Khurgee]] illustrates the different stages. The June 1997 FAQ and April 1998 Current Rulings limited his search ability to once per control phase. Glossary 2.0 then incorporated that limit directly into his [[Captain Khurgee (Errata)|replacement game text]]. The earlier ruling and the later revised text are separate events in the card’s history.<ref name="faq97-history" /><ref name="cr98-history" /><ref name="glossary-history" />

=== 1999–2000: balance changes and a combined online reference ===

The consolidated books continued to receive updates. Decipher’s '''January 1999 errata notice''' addressed dominant tournament strategies through both a revised operative rule and changes to individual cards. On their matching planets, operatives could not supply ability for battle destiny or control a location alone; another card or cards with total ability of at least 1 were required for control. Duplicate operatives of the same title also faced deployment and movement restrictions. The notice explained the gameplay problems behind its changes.<ref name="errata99-history">[http://decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/faqs/errata012099.html Errata: January 1999], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990422144919/http://decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/faqs/errata012099.html Internet Archive].</ref>

The online '''Glossary and Current Rules, Version 2.1''', updated '''1 October 1999''', combined Glossary 2.0, the Enhanced Premiere and Endor rulesheets and the September 1999 Current Rulings in one alphabetical reference. Online publication now also provided a consolidated reading reference alongside the separate printed and downloadable documents.<ref name="online99-history">[http://decipher.com/starwars/rules/glossary/index.html Online Glossary and Current Rules, Version 2.1], Decipher (updated 1 October 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991012154128/http://decipher.com/starwars/rules/glossary/index.html Internet Archive].</ref>

=== 2001–2002: the Glossary Supplement and dated changes ===

The '''30 May 2001 Supplement to Glossary''' collected updates, corrections, new rulings and rule notes from products released after Special Edition. Its entries replaced the corresponding Glossary entries unless they explicitly supplemented them. Its symbols distinguished changes in gameplay or understanding from material reproduced or rearranged from earlier documents.<ref name="supplement01-history">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgsupplement053001.pdf Supplement to Glossary], Decipher (30 May 2001), p. 1. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010613012725/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgsupplement053001.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

The [[Decipher Glossary Supplement|29 January 2002 Glossary Supplement]] retained this layered system. It told players to consult the supplement first and separated newly changed gameplay from clarification and previously published material. Its preface also specified a later effective date for marked gameplay changes, allowing players and tournament directors time to prepare. Publication dates and effective dates could therefore differ.<ref name="supplement02-history">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgglossarysupplement.pdf Glossary Supplement], Decipher (updated 29 January 2002), p. 1. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041106202626/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgglossarysupplement.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

=== The Players Committee: supplements and the Advanced Rulebook ===

The [[Players Committee Rules Supplement (2003)|27 January 2003 PC Rules Supplement]] explicitly supplemented Decipher’s Rulebook and Glossary 2.0 and its January 2002 supplement. It instructed players to check the most recent document first, with newer entries replacing older ones unless stated otherwise. It also addressed Virtual cards, bringing the continuing game into the inherited rules framework.<ref name="pc03-history">[http://www.theforce.net/ccg/vcards/SWCCGRules01-27-03.pdf Star Wars CCG Rules Supplement], Players Committee (27 January 2003), pp. 1–2. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030822212619/http://www.theforce.net/ccg/vcards/SWCCGRules01-27-03.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

The PC subsequently organized its '''Advanced Rulebook''' around gameplay topics and worked examples. [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook 1.7.1|Version 1.7.1]] in 2007 explained that the accumulated rules had become difficult to navigate and that the book brought them together with explanations of how they worked. [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook 2.0|Version 2.0]] continued this approach in 2012. Its chapters cover core procedures, card types, special rules and battle, followed by appendices for errata, card rulings and other references.<ref name="pc-history" /><ref name="pc12-history">Players Committee, [[Media:AR-version-2-0-final.pdf|Advanced Rulebook 2.0]] (2012), contents and introduction, printed pp. i–vi.</ref>

The [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook|2023 Advanced Rulebook]] retains a chapter-based rules reference with separate appendices for errata and card rulings. The PC also publishes a shorter Beginner’s Rulebook for learning the game.<ref name="advanced" /><ref name="beginner" />

<gallery mode="packed" heights="160">
File:PC-AR-2023-page-001.png|Players Committee Advanced Rulebook, 2023 edition.
</gallery>

''Rule'', ''ruling'' and ''errata'' describe different kinds of information within this history. A supplement can introduce a new procedure; a ruling can explain an interaction; and errata can replace a card’s text. Glossaries and advanced rulebooks bring these kinds of material together, while later dated updates continue to change particular entries.<ref name="faq97-history" /><ref name="glossary-history" /><ref name="supplement02-history" />

== How the documents fit together ==

* '''Rulebooks''' explain the game’s procedures. '''Glossaries''' supply detailed definitions and card entries.
* '''Rulesheets and supplements''' add expansion mechanics or update earlier documents. Use them with the core book for their period.
* '''Errata''' publish changed card text. '''FAQs and Current Rulings''' record historical answers and interpretations; a document may also contain separately identified errata.
* '''Tournament guides''' address organized-play procedures alongside gameplay rules.
* '''Wiki reading copies''' make individual documents readable here. The [[Decipher Comprehensive Rules]] is a wiki compilation of Decipher material rather than a separately issued Decipher book.

For example, [[Special Edition]] paired Rulebook 2.0 with Glossary 2.0 in November 1998. Later rulesheets and the [[Decipher Glossary Supplement|Glossary Supplement]] added material to that reference.<ref name="se">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/rules/index.html Star Wars Customizable Card Game: Rules], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990428184433/http://www.decipher.com:80/starwars/productlibrary/rules/index.html Internet Archive, 28 April 1999].</ref> A late-era compilation is not the starting ruleset for every earlier expansion.
